UntimedRoiAnalysis.Kind: Untimed structural count for a proposed common-Y-range ablation
Method: Use every Candidate=true pair in validation.json, retaining both directions; no pair is selected by time, output quality or shape.
Read the unchanged binary64 coordinate arrays from the frozen source files. For each pair let lo=max(minY(zone),minY(query)), hi=min(maxY(zone),maxY(query)).

Sort distinct endpoint Y values from both rings. OriginalBands is the number of distinct levels minus one and is asserted equal to the measured BandCount for every candidate. All these source rings have active edges between their extreme Y values.

RestrictedBands is the number of distinct endpoint Y values in the inclusive [lo,hi] interval minus one. Both bounds already occur among the source endpoint levels; no constructed crossing levels or quantized coordinates are introduced.

InitialActiveEdges counts all implicit-closure segments satisfying min(endpointY)<=lo<max(endpointY), separately across both rings. Horizontal edges contribute zero. This is the status immediately above the lower bound.

Summary counts are simple sums; medians are the sorted middle value, or mean of the two middle values for even populations. Every candidate count row is retained in the archived roi-analysis.json; the public manifest includes the summaries.
Interpretation: This is potential endpoint-band reduction, not a timed implementation or CPU-time saving estimate. It does not count how many inner active visits or area terms an actual restricted sweep would perform.

A correct restricted implementation must initialize every spanning edge at lo, certify their just-above order and establish both winding prefixes before sweeping; original input validation, edge preparation and initial status sorting remain necessary.
Do not prune X-side edges without preserving their winding contributions. Keep all interval/error/fallback contracts, exact-oracle tests, frozen inputs and the declared performance gates.

The current 7.8-8.0x Clipper and 10.2-11.0x Winding full-query loss is not explained quantitatively by these counts. Scalar-filter and interval-arithmetic CPU shares require a separate profile or controlled ablation.
Input geometry, shipping code and measured binaries are unchanged. No new benchmarks were run for this analysis.
